column1: # Game profile of LEGO® Harry Potter™ Collection (010052A00B5D2000), update 1.0.2 (v131072), SDK 5.4.0.
# TT Games' own renderer: the Windows D3D11 DLLs ported to nn::ro modules. main is 750 instructions that mount the
# RomFS; libHarryLauncher.nro (nro2) starts and loads libharry1.nro (nro1, Years 1-4) or libharry2.nro (nro0,
# Years 5-7) as a module — lhp_switch_dll_launcher.nrr registers all three. Modules main, sdk and those three NROs
# are rewritten, and the host maps the NROs at start (loader.c, "NRO modules").
# Years 5-7's frame is built by three routines this build does not order as the console does, and that is the crash
# this profile's one cut fixes: the recorder stores a pass's record in the live table at singleton+0x9d0
# (nro0+0xd2ff0), the begin-frame routine copies the 24 entries into the published table at singleton+0xa90 a frame
# phase later (nro0+0x15f420), and the replay reads the published table in the same frame (nro0+0xd39c0 and eleven
# other sites) — different threads, two locks that do not order them. patches.py publishes the record at the store
# (nro0+0xd3138); dm/host/hle_nullpass.c reads a load that still faults in the null page as zero for the sites a
# frame reaches before it fills them (the emulator's recovery, natively).
# What this profile does NOT hold: the shader tables. They are the build's own output (the derived profile), and 493
# of the map's rows come from a run-time dump no split reproduces (docs/reference/shaders.md, "Shaders whose bytes
# exist only in a run-time dump"). The note says where they are and what each count is.
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon
